issues.claim: R5-03 rewrote §4.11 *The clock* (4) (l. 8476–8487). A calamity dated at or before the last epoch's week `W₀` is late. Where the absorb's week `W₁` is after `W₀`, "it rides the first epoch this absorb folds … its `EpochInputs.events` entry at that epoch's first week `W₀` + 1". Only where `W₁` is not after `W₀` does it fold no epoch: it is then "held in the binding (`DossierBinding.lateCalamities`, §7.7) until the first epoch a later absorb folds". So the one late calamity with no epoch event is a held one. V01 glosses the no-event case the other way at four sites, and R5-03's sweep did not name V01. The sites are §3.16 (2) (l. 2337–2339: "so a calamity carried with no event (one dated at or before the last absorbed week) still gives its targets and its pattern"), §3.18's disaster row (l. 2678), T-V1-60 (d) (l. 3363) and J-V1.104 (l. 3627). The last three read "a … calamity carried with no epoch event (dated at or before the last absorbed week)". The gloss is wrong for the ordinary absorb (`W₁` after `W₀`), and "the last absorbed week" is no term of the base. V01 reads the carried fact either way, so the units are unchanged. But T-V1-60 (d)'s fixture built to the gloss rides an epoch event, so the clause's named case (no epoch event) is never run.
issues.required_change: V01 §3.16 (2): "so a calamity carried with no event (one dated at or before the last absorbed week) still gives its targets and its pattern" → "so a calamity carried with no epoch event yet — a late one held in `DossierBinding.lateCalamities` until a later absorb's epoch (§4.11 *The clock* (4)) — still gives its targets and its pattern". §3.18's disaster row: "a linked calamity carried with no epoch event (dated at or before the last absorbed week)" → "a linked calamity carried with no epoch event yet (a late one held in `DossierBinding.lateCalamities`, §4.11 *The clock* (4))". T-V1-60 (d): "a linked calamity carried with no epoch event (dated at or before the last absorbed week) strikes its targets, with its pattern" → "a linked calamity carried late by a second absorb in the last epoch's own week, held in `DossierBinding.lateCalamities` with no epoch event (§4.11 *The clock* (4)), strikes its targets, with its pattern, as does one carried late by an absorb whose week is after the last epoch's (riding that absorb's first epoch)". J-V1.104: "a calamity carried with no epoch event (dated at or before the last absorbed week)" → "a calamity carried with no epoch event yet (a late one held in `DossierBinding.lateCalamities`, §4.11 *The clock* (4))".

issues.claim: R5-02 lets a wall stretch laid after a raised way run on beneath its deck. In §2.7's support step (6) (d) (l. 2603–2616), "beneath every other span it is an ordinary run whose top is no higher than that span's soffit (the arch walled up …)". So a later ring passing under a viaduct or an aqueduct stands a wall run under an `open` span. V01 §3.17.3 (2) (l. 2464–2470) still describes the under-deck strip's spans as "the base's arch vaults (II.7.6; volume 4's `vault` spans) fill it where they exist, and an `open` span stays open ground, a way passing under it or bare ground". R5-02's sweep listed V01 §3.17.3 (3) and l. 978, 1424, 2485, not (2). V01 lays nothing in the strip, so nothing V01 builds changes.
issues.required_change: V01 §3.17.3 (2): "and an `open` span stays open ground, a way passing under it or bare ground" → "and an `open` span stays open ground, a way passing under it, bare ground or the run of a wall stretch laid after the raised way, walled up beneath it (§2.7's support step (6) (d))" (the quotation of item 110 (b) after it kept).

issues.claim: R5-02 makes the commit that creates a raised way load-bearing. Its stations, keys and spans are placed there and held from then. §2.7's support step (6) (l. 2580–2583) names that commit: "at generation inside S4's or a stage's S5b route solve or at S6's end". §4.3 *The slot* (l. 5719–5722: "a viaduct inside S4's route solve (and each later stage's S5b through this router)") and V11 §3.24.2's readers (l. 3903–3904) say the same. V01 §3.17.4 (l. 2495–2496) lists the generated raised parts' commits as "— the viaduct inside S4's route solve, the elevated road and the aqueduct at S6's end (item 290)" and leaves out S5b's viaduct. Its claim that they are all committed before S7b (1) holds for S5b too, so nothing built changes.
issues.required_change: V01 §3.17.4: "— the viaduct inside S4's route solve, the elevated road and the aqueduct at S6's end (item 290)" → "— a viaduct inside S4's route solve or a later stage's S5b, the elevated road and the aqueduct at S6's end (item 290; §2.7's support step (6))".

issues.claim: repair-r5-V02's HAND-OFFS (its one end for round-5 verifiers, no END line naming it) asks V03 §3.13's damage-layer row (l. 2094) to give the entry week in its level-1 outcome. The row's outcome cell still reads "every element damaged at 1". V02's own row on the same case now reads "every element the plan holds damaged, each from its entry week into the plan (V03 §5.6 (2) (a))" (V02 §3.18 l. 2519). The home, V03 §5.6 (2) (a), reads "an element is compared with the level only from its entry week". So V03's own edge row disagrees in form with its home and with V02's row. Nothing built changes.
issues.required_change: V03 §3.13's damage-layer row, outcome cell: "every element damaged at 1" → "every element damaged at 1, each from its entry week into the plan (V03 §5.6 (2) (a))".

issues.claim: One fix with VRC5T-03, at a site that issue does not list. R5-04 conditioned the no-op: §6.3 *Plan damage* (l. 10010–10011) reads "a building never decayed and under no disaster look (§2.6 step 7) draws its plan unchanged (`item123.damage`)", and §8.6 (l. 14157) says the same. V03 §5.2's SVG paragraph (l. 2488) ends the `plan.damage` group's rule with "absent when nothing is damaged or repaired, so a building never decayed exports byte-identically". Its next sentences (l. 2491–2492) make a picture export draw the damage "as the view does, a disaster's look included (item 122 (f))". So a never-decayed building under a disaster look exports the group, and the conclusion states the unconditioned form. The sentence after it decides the case, so nothing built changes.
issues.required_change: V03 §5.2: "so a building never decayed exports byte-identically" → "so a building never decayed and under no disaster look (§6.3 *Plan damage*) exports byte-identically".
